reason: Starts with an action, names the event and names the physical product. The subhead supplies the three use cases and low-power/offline benefits.

changes.before: Put a changing code at the point of work.
changes.after: Record check-ins with a rotating QR display.

changes.before: Give your team a compact point to scan for a shift, a room or a visit.
changes.after: Check workers into shifts, rooms and home visits. Put a small, low-power display where they need to scan, even when connectivity drops.

changes.before: Explore the uses
changes.after: Explore check-in options

changes.before: A dedicated display for one clear task.
changes.after: Place it where your team checks in.

changes.before: Give every shift a clear check-in point.
changes.after: See who checks in for each shift.

changes.before: Place the display at the entrance or team check-in area. Workers scan the current code in the app to connect the event to the person, site and time.
changes.after: Put the display at your entrance or staff check-in point. Workers scan the current code in the Certifyd app. You see who checked in, where and when.

changes.before: Rotating, time-limited codes help prevent an old screenshot from being reused for a later check-in. Keep check-in and check-out events connected to the worker record.
changes.after: Follow check-in and check-out in the worker’s record. Time-limited codes help stop workers reusing an old screenshot for a later scan.

changes.before: Connect a visit to the room where it happens.
changes.after: Track check-ins to each care-home room.

changes.before: Put a compact display at the relevant room or care point. The scan records which point the worker checked into and when.
changes.after: Place a display by the room or care point. Each scan adds the worker, room and time to the visit record.

changes.before: Give the care team a room-level event to review alongside the wider visit and shift history. Keep resident information out of the code itself.
changes.after: Review room check-ins alongside the wider shift history. Keep resident details out of the QR code.

changes.before: Record the visit at the home.
changes.after: Record home visits, even without a connection.

changes.before: Leave a dedicated display at the agreed check-in point. The worker scans it on arrival and at the relevant points in the visit workflow.
changes.after: Leave a small display at the agreed point in the home. Care workers scan on arrival and at the other points your visit process requires.

changes.before: Offline operation supports visits where connectivity is unreliable. The app queues the event and syncs it when a connection returns.
changes.after: Keep recording when the connection drops. The app saves the scan and syncs it when the worker reconnects.

changes.before: Use a QR display where a tablet is more than you need.
changes.after: Replace a check-in tablet with a compact display.

changes.before: The display has one job: present the current code. A smaller, dedicated device is designed to cost less than putting an iPad at every check-in point.
changes.after: Put a lower-cost device at each check-in point. The display shows the changing code; workers use their own phones to scan it.

changes.before: Low-power operation and a compact enclosure make it suitable for entrances, rooms and home visits without turning each point into a kiosk.
changes.after: Fit it beside an entrance, a room door or a home-visit point. Its small enclosure and low power use help you place more scan points where your team needs them.

changes.before: One job. A smaller footprint.
changes.after: Keep each check-in point small.

changes.before: A changing code, a clear location and a worker using the app. Keep the hardware focused on that moment.
changes.after: Mount the display. Assign the location. Let your team scan with the app.

changes.before: Follow the scan into the worker’s record.
changes.after: Connect each scan to a person, place and time.

changes.before: The device is one part of the system. Connect the place, the person and the recorded event in Certifyd.
changes.after: Give your managers a record they can review. Follow each check-in from the assigned display to the worker’s record in Certifyd.

changes.before: Review the recorded activity.
changes.after: Review each check-in.

changes.before: Follow the person, point and time, including queued offline events.
changes.after: See the worker, location and time. Follow saved offline scans as they sync.

changes.before: Show us where your team needs to check in.
changes.after: Plan your shift and care check-in points.

changes.after: Tell us where your team works. We’ll walk through where to put the displays, how workers scan and what your managers need to see.

claim_boundaries: User-supplied lower-cost and low-power benefits; no invented price or battery hours.
Rotating codes help against stale screenshots; they do not alone prove continuous presence or stop live relays.
Examples are fictional; no customer proof or testimonials.
scope: Physical rotating QR mockup. Wider website review remains in progress.
